extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant writers (nonprofit staff, academic researchers, government applicants) and people learning how to prepare funding proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Writing proposals to obtain financial support from foundations, government, corporations, or other funders; covers components, sector conventions, and quality criteria for successful applications across academic, nonprofit, and government contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter / Letter of intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of organization or PI; statement of need; brief project description; amount requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used as the initial contact; should succinctly introduce the applicant and the request. Keep concise and targeted to funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project summary / Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1-page overview that states the problem, solution, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often the most-read section of an application — make it clear, compelling, and self-contained. Use plain language to convey significance and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of need
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents the problem to be addressed, cites credible data, establishes urgency, and connects the need to funder priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and statistics, explain who is affected and why intervention is required now. Avoid vague statements; explicitly tie the need to the funder's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project description / Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed account of the project including goals and objectives, methodology, timeline, personnel, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure clearly (e.g., goals → methods → timeline → staffing → outcomes). Include enough methodological detail to demonstrate feasibility and rigor; make activities and deliverables explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific, measurable aims the project intends to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be concrete and measurable (SMART-style implicitly endorsed). Distinguish between broad goals and actionable objectives tied to evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific methods and procedures by which the project will accomplish its objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness for the objectives. For research grants emphasize hypothesis-driven or argument-driven logic as appropriate; explain why chosen methods are best.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A realistic schedule for project activities and deliverables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, feasible timeline that aligns with scope and budget; unrealistic timelines are a common weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel / Investigator qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of key staff, their roles, and relevant qualifications or productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For academic proposals highlight investigator productivity and institutional environment; for nonprofits emphasize organizational capacity. Include CVs/resumes in supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of personnel, direct costs, indirect costs (where allowed), and narrative justification for expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets must be realistic and aligned with project scope. Justify major line items, follow funder rules on indirect costs, and ensure totals match narrative needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget alignment with scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget should be proportional and realistic relative to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inflated or underestimated budgets; reviewers assess whether requested funds are necessary and sufficient to achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan and outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for measuring outcomes, data collection, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific, measurable metrics and methods for assessing impact. Strong evaluation plans are frequently highlighted as a distinguishing feature of competitive proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support, compliance approvals, organizational documents, CVs, and other attachments required by the funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required documents are complete and current. Letters of support should be specific and concrete (not generic); missing or weak attachments are common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional presentation and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, persuasive, specific writing and professional formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polished prose, correct grammar, consistent formatting, and attention to detail signal competence. Presentation includes adherence to page limits and formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with funder priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the proposal maps onto the funder's stated goals, priorities, and interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funder guidelines and tailor the proposal. For foundations, program officer engagement and prior conversations can be valuable; proposals that mismatch priorities fare poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funder rules and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to strict formatting, documentation, eligibility, and submission rules (especially common in government grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow RFAs and solicitations exactly. Many government grants have multi-stage review processes and strict compliance checks; format violations or missing required documents can disqualify an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timeliness and administrative completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting by the deadline with all required components and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions or missing documents are frequent reasons for rejection. Plan for internal reviews and institutional approvals to meet deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of how the project or its benefits will continue after the grant period (often emphasized in nonprofit proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for ongoing funding, institutionalization, or scalability. Funders often prefer projects with clear prospects for sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic model / program theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear causal model linking inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes (commonly used in nonprofit proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logic models to demonstrate how activities lead to intended outcomes and inform evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific conventions — Academic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic proposals typically include Specific Aims, hypothesis-driven or argument-driven structure, emphasis on investigator productivity and institutional environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow discipline norms (e.g., Specific Aims page for NIH/NSF). Emphasize publications, prior work, and institutional resources that support project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific conventions — Nonprofit grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit proposals emphasize statement of need with community data, goals/objectives, logic models, sustainability, and organizational capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate community engagement, capacity to deliver services, and how interventions address stated needs. Include letters demonstrating partnerships or community buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific conventions — Government grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Government funding often has strict format requirements, compliance-heavy documentation, multi-stage review, and formal evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow solicitations (RFAs) and compliance rules; expect formal scoring criteria and possible required forms or certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific conventions — Foundations, corporations, and crowdfunding
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations value alignment with priorities and may prefer prior engagement or letters of inquiry; corporations emphasize cause-marketing fit and local/employee engagement; crowdfunding relies on storytelling and community outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor approach: cultivate relationships and LOIs for foundations, highlight community or branding fit for corporations, and use narrative + multimedia for crowdfunding campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder engagement and relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-submission engagement with program officers or foundation staff and relationship cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal pre-engagement (e.g., LOIs, conversations) can help assess fit and increase competitiveness. For foundations, trust relationships often matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer skills and professionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Required skills include research and analysis, writing and editing, project management, knowledge of the funder landscape, and attention to detail; grant writing is a professionalized career path with certifications and compensation norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop domain knowledge, editing skills, and project-management practices. Professional credentials (e.g., Grant Professionals Association) may indicate expertise but are not universally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common pitfalls / anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent weaknesses such as vague problem statements, mismatched funder priorities, unrealistic budgets, missing evaluation plans, missing documents, format violations, late submissions, and generic letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist of common pitfalls to self-audit proposals. Address each potential weakness proactively (e.g., quantify need, align goals, justify budget, draft specific letters of support).
